messages.author: 37abdbe6ce54889a
messages.subject: BYM model with varying intercept
parts:
Hi Dear INLA Experts:

I've recently got a data, say, 36 regions and 127 copies, in other words for each fips I have 127 measurements (The data dimension is 127*36).
And the 127 measures are independent, so it's not space-time problem.

I want to fit a model like this:

f2=y~1 + f(fips, model="bym", graph=adj)

I want to use all the 127 measurements to estimate the mu vector of the 36 regions , in the mean time I want to impose the CAR type structure in the covariance structure,  

Since I want each region has its own intercept, is it right to create dummy variables for each region ? 


f2=y~dummy1+...dummy35 + f(fips, model="bym", graph=adj)


I'm not sure if this is the right way to model this, cause usually we have a 2-D data, now I think it's a 3-D data.


Any suggestion is greatly appreciated ! 

Thanks so much in advance !


Xiao

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] BYM model with varying intercept
parts:
On 10/02/16 18:23, Xiao Li wrote:
>
> Since I want each region has its own intercept, is it right to create
> dummy variables for each region ?

You can consider the time index as a factor covariate and them use
y ~ time + f(fips, model="bym", graph=adj)

You can also define a random effect over time, based on the integer time
index
y ~ f(time, ...) + f(fips, model="bym", graph=adj)


Elias

yes. use a factor with one level for each region. 

if you want the spatial component be independent for each replication,
but share the same hyperparameter, then use 'replicate=...'.

While in the second model, there are actually 127*36 random effects.

If I consider one copy of 36 region measurement as "one person", can I interpret these 127*36 random effects as 127 copies of 'subject effect', each subject has a set of 36 region effect. And all these total measurements convey the information of the shared parameter and hyperparameters ?


Thanks !


Xiao
